summary: Janice Leoshko is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She completed her doctoral studies under Susan L. Huntington and became Professor Emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin, attested in 2026.

Jann Ronis specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Virginia, studying under David Germano, Jeffrey Hopkins, and Sonam Tenpa, and held an attested post there in 2007.

Jared Rhoton (1941–1993) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga and completed his dissertation at Columbia University in 1985 under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman.

Jarl Charpentier (1884–1935) was a Swedish Indologist and linguist. He studied at Uppsala University and the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi, later serving at Uppsala as Assistant Professor (1908), Deputy Professor (1925), and Professor (1927).

Jaromír Borecký (1869–1951) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the Faculty of Arts, Charles University in Prague (~1888–1892), and served as Director of the National Library of the Czech Republic (~1920–1939).
Jaromír Jedlička (1869–1901) was a Czech linguist and Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. under Josef Zubatý at Charles University, where he also worked as a library worker in 1899.
Jaroslav Průšek (1906–1980) was a Czech sinologist. He pursued his studies at Charles University's Faculty of Arts in Prague between approximately 1924 and 1928.

Jason Birch is an Indologist who earned his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts as Senior Research Fellow at SOAS University of London (2015–2024) and Research Associate at Oxford (2024).

Jason Hawkes is an archaeologist and Indologist who earned his PhD from Cambridge. He has held positions including Finds Manager and Lecturer at Cambridge, Project Curator at the British Museum (2014–2020), and Bye-Fellow at Gonville and Caius College (2021).

Jason M. Wirth (born 1963) works in philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Kosho Itagaki (attested 2017–2019) and became a professor at Seattle University in 2005.

Jason Matthew McCombs is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his BS from the University of Michigan and his PhD from UCLA under Gregory Schopen, subsequently serving as a lecturer at UCLA.

Jason Neelis works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington under Richard G. Salomon and held posts at the University of Florida (2003–2010) and Wilfrid Laurier University (from 2010).

Jason Protass specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD from Stanford University under John Kieschnick and held posts as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University and a Fulbright Fellow at Academia Sinica.

Javana Ñāṇa works in Buddhist studies, earning degrees from the National University of Mongolia, ITBMU, Shan State Buddhist University, and the University of Kelaniya. In 2025, he served as a Bhikkhu at Shan State Buddhist University.

Jay Holt Valentine specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Kurtis R. Schaeffer and became an Associate Professor at Troy University in 2015.

Jay Jasanoff (born 1942) is a linguist and Indologist who earned his bachelor's degree at Harvard University. He was Professor of Linguistics at Cornell (1981–1985) before becoming Diebold Professor of Indo-European Linguistics and Philology at Harvard in 1998.

Jay L. Garfield (born 1955) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has served as Doris Silbert Professor Emeritus at Smith College, with additional appointments at Hampshire College, the University of Massachusetts Amherst, the University of Melbourne, and CIHTS.
Jayadevbhai Mohanlal Shukla was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar and served as Reader of Sanskrit at Gujarat University.

Jayandra Soni (born 1947) is an Indologist and philosopher who earned PhDs from Banaras Hindu University and McMaster University. He served as a lecturer at the University of Marburg (1991–2012) and Generalsekretär of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies (2012).

Jayanta Acharya is an Indologist who completed a PhD at Nepal Sanskrit University (2018–2022). He became a professor at Nepal Sanskrit University in 1997 and served as a SPOC for the International Astronomical Union from 2009 to 2018.
